title: Keep a balance and its transaction count consistent

blocks.text: When two fields must always agree, updating them one after the other is an atomicity violation: a reader can see the new balance with the old transaction count. The page's first fix (its `MultiVariableAtomicity`, approach 1) guards **every** read and write of both fields with one lock: `synchronized` methods on the object.
Write `Account`, with a balance and a count of successful transactions, both starting at 0. Guard both fields with the account object's own monitor (`synchronized` methods, or `synchronized (this)`):

items: `deposit(amount)` adds to the balance and counts one transaction;
`withdraw(amount)` takes from the balance and counts one transaction, or returns `false` and changes nothing when the balance is too small;
`snapshot()` returns a `Snapshot(balance, transactions)` read in one step.

cases.says: Deposits and withdrawals move the balance and each counts one transaction, and a snapshot reads both.
A withdrawal larger than the balance is refused and changes neither field.
A deposit waits while another thread holds the account's lock, so both fields change in one step.
withdraw() waits while another thread holds the account's own monitor, like every other update.
A snapshot waits for the lock too, so it never pairs a new balance with an old count.

concepts: Fields that must stay consistent are all read and written under one lock, so no reader sees half an update.
